how_customers_find_and_choose: Shoppers search the map listing first, then read recent reviews and look at photos before visiting
Customers ask in chat for availability, a photo or a video of the item before they travel
Comparing the same item across several sellers online is routine, so a clear listing and honest stock answers decide the sale
Recommendations from friends and family shared in chat groups still carry the most weight
Short vertical videos of new arrivals help fashion, decor, gifts and gadgets where the owner already has something to show
what_works_now: A product catalogue shared in chat with clear photos, plain names and an in-stock note
A complete map listing: correct hours, location pin, phone and recent photos
Asking happy customers for a review at the counter or right after delivery
A chat reply within minutes during opening hours, with a saved short answer for common questions
Simple repeat-customer contact: a saved list of regulars told when stock they like arrives
Honest delivery promises and a clear return or exchange rule said up front
Counting what sells each week and not reordering what sits
outdated_or_weak: Printing flyers or pamphlets as the main way to reach people
Waiting for walk-in footfall alone with no online presence
A website built once and never updated while the map listing is incomplete
Generic advice to 'post daily on social media' with nothing specific to show
Blanket discounts that train customers to wait for the next sale
Mass messages to everyone, whether or not they asked for them

PK: Cash on delivery and cash at the counter are still common; bank transfer and mobile wallet payments are now normal for many customers
Ramadan and the two Eids reshape demand, opening hours and staff availability every year
Summer heat, monsoon rain and power cuts affect operations and footfall
Customers often write in Urdu, Roman Urdu or a regional language, and chat is the usual first contact
Cash on delivery returns and refused parcels are a real cost for sellers who deliver
Seasonal peaks: Eid, weddings and back-to-school drive buying
UAE: Customers are multilingual and expect quick replies in chat; card and tap payments are normal
Winter is the busy season; many residents travel in summer so demand can dip
Ramadan and Eid change hours and buying patterns; the licence a business holds decides what it may sell and advertise, so the owner checks that with the licensing body
Tourist and expat footfall matters in malls and souks; shoppers expect chat support in several languages
Seasonal sale periods and gifting occasions are well established
CA: Customers expect online booking or enquiry, card and bank e-transfer payment, and clear written confirmation
Long winters and a short summer peak shape outdoor and seasonal trades
English and French (in Quebec) matter, and many communities prefer their own language; consent for marketing messages and sales tax rules vary, so the owner checks them with a professional
Customers compare local shops with online delivery from large sellers, so local service and fast pickup are the edge
Holiday gifting and back-to-school are the big retail seasons

never_assume: A social page with a real following
A stock list kept anywhere other than the owner's head or a notebook
Delivery staff or a courier arrangement
